afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 300514
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1014 PM MST Thu Oct 29 2026

.UPDATE...Updated 06z Aviation Discussion...

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A Flood Watch remains in effect for portions of south-central
  and eastern Arizona for Friday.

- Showers and thunderstorms, some producing moderate to heavy
  rainfall, are expected on Friday centered over south-central
  Arizona. Localized rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are likely. 

- Sunday will again bring flooding concerns as additional rainfall
  amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected from Phoenix and areas to
  the north and east of Phoenix. 

- A Flood Watch has been issued for portions of south-central and
  eastern Arizona for Sunday.
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Friday/... 
Today will be the last dry and calm weather day ahead of the next
couple of weather systems that will bring rainy weather starting 
Friday and expected to last through the holiday weekend. A large 
trough is currently positioned off the western coast, with a cut-
off low developing along the coast of Washington. Additionally, a 
near climatological record strong west to east subtropical jet is 
stretched from northeast Hawaii to just west of the Baja coast. 
This jet will play a pivotal role in how much rainfall we can 
expect over the next several days, especially on Sunday as it will
drive a strong atmospheric river into our region.

As mentioned the rest of today will continue to be quiet, with 
increasing cloud coverage throughout the rest of the day as the 
southwesterly flow aloft is already beginning to be advected into
the region ahead of the large scale trough over the west coast. 
By Friday PWATs will be near 200-250% of normal, and while the 
troughing feature will remain positioned off the west coast, a 
shortwave will track through the Desert SW Friday afternoon. This 
shortwave will aid in providing enough ascent for showers and 
thunderstorms to develop starting as early as Friday morning. 
Forecast soundings and the latest HREF guidance continue to point 
towards good elevated instability developing across south-central 
Arizona tonight into Friday, potentially leading to MUCAPEs of 
over 1000 J/kg in a small corridor from central Pima County 
through western Pinal into northern Maricopa Counties. Latest Hi- 
res CAMs show show showers developing as early as 5-7AM however 
activity is expected to be light early Friday morning. The main 
window for widespread showers and thunderstorms won't be until 
late morning/ early afternoon, where a few severe storms will be 
possible, as SPC did upgrade the region from general thunderstorms
to a Marginal risk for severe weather Friday for south-central 
and southeastern AZ. 
  
Storm totals Friday are forecasted to generally be between 0.5-1.00" 
centered over and just northeast of Phoenix. However, localized 
amounts of up to around 2" are definitely possible with any severe 
or training storms. With the expected totals a Floor Watch remains 
in effect for Maricopa County, portions of NW Pinal County starting 
Friday morning, then expanding into Gila County by the late morning 
hours. 

Otherwise, temperatures today will be very similar to the last few 
days with highs mostly in the mid 80s across the lower deserts, 
despite the periods of thicker high clouds. The increased clouds and 
the periods of rain on Friday should hold daytime highs to at most 
75 degrees in the Phoenix area, while the western lower deserts will 
only dip down to around 80 degrees for highs.

&&

.LONG TERM /Saturday through Wednesday/... 
A short drying period will move in on Saturday, but higher level
moisture and clouds will be increasing throughout the day. We 
can't rule out a few light showers on Saturday, but with little to
no instability and drier air in the mid levels little if any 
additional accumulating rainfall is expected through at least the 
afternoon. Some guidance is showing shower activity to begin 
already in the evening, but for most areas it should hold off 
until after midnight.

Attention then turns toward one of our stronger Arv that can
affect the Desert Southwest moving in Saturday night and lasting
through much of Sunday. The AR will also coincide with a fairly 
strong shortwave trough developing west of northern Baja on 
Saturday before tracking right through the southern half of 
Arizona during the daytime hours Sunday. This weather event is
shaping up to be a classic El Nino season AR event which would
normally occur from late December through February. All of the
ingredients for a prolonged moderate rainfall event look to be
there on Sunday with an impressive 18 hours of 35-50kt
southwesterly upslope H8-H7 flow and at least 12 hours of strong 
jet forced ascent. These impressive forcing mechanisms will also 
line up with record or near record moisture levels for this time 
of year with PWATs rising to 300-350% of normal. Instability will 
be lacking with MUCAPEs at most 200-300 J/kg, but the long 
duration of the rain will make up for the lack of higher rainfall 
rates. 

We expect showers to blossom first over the high terrain northeast
of Phoenix sometime in the evening before filling in across most 
of south-central Arizona around or just after midnight. Showers 
will stay somewhat scattered through the overnight hours before 
becoming widespread over much of Arizona by mid morning Sunday. As
the main shortwave begins to track through southern California 
later Sunday morning, a fairly solid shield of light to moderate 
rain should move through southern California and then through 
Arizona Sunday afternoon. Upslope showers should persist over 
portions of south-central Arizona into the high terrain into 
Sunday evening, but the activity should be gradually winding down.

Expected rainfall rates on Sunday are not all that high, but rain
totals will add up over time as this event will last longer than
our typical weather events. Based on the record moisture levels, 
strong forcing, but little instability rainfall rates will 
generally be in the 0.1-0.2"/hr range in the Phoenix area to as 
high as 0.2-0.3"/hr in the high terrain north and east of the 
Phoenix area. Fairly steady light to moderate rainfall is expected
from just before sunrise through the afternoon in the 
aforementioned areas with rainfall totals averaging 1-1.5" in 
Phoenix to 2-3" over the higher terrain. Believe it our not, the 
NBM is also suggesting the possibility (25%) of rainfall totals 
over 2" in the Phoenix to as much as 3-4" in the high terrain. 
Much lower rainfall totals of 0.25-0.5" are expected over the 
lower deserts of southwest Arizona and southeast California due to
some rain-shadowing effects and the lack of upslope forcing.

Even if the average forecast rainfall totals come to fruition on
Sunday, the bulk of the rain will runoff as it will be falling on
already saturated soils. In turn another Flood Watch has been
issued for a large area of south-central AZ, and the eastern AZ 
high terrain starting Sunday, into Monday morning. During this 
time we anticipate the potential for many of the washes filling or
overflowing, and flooding in some of the larger creeks and rivers
as all of the expected rain works through the water basins.

Dry air will begin to filter into the region from the northwest
later on Sunday, overspreading the bulk of the area by Monday 
morning. We may have some lingering showers across the eastern 
1/3rd of Arizona Sunday night into Monday morning, but additional
rainfall amounts should be fairly light. The rest of Monday will
bring decreasing clouds as the drier air works into the region
while another follow-on shortwave trough moves southeastward into
northern New Mexico. Temperatures for both Sunday and Monday will
be fairly cool with highs as low as the lower 70s for the Phoenix
area to maybe the mid to upper 70s across the western lower 
deserts. Upper level ridging is then forecast to mostly take over 
across the Desert Southwest going into the middle part of next 
week, but temperatures will be fairly slow to rise with readings 
staying below normal.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0510Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT; 
Thunderstorm activity with gusty and erratic winds as well 
lowered CIGs and VIS due to heavy rainfall Friday afternoon will 
be the main aviation weather issues throughout the TAF period. In 
the meantime, quiet conditions will prevail through at least early
Friday morning. Easterly winds will prevail throughout much of the
period with speeds aob 10 kts. Areas of VCSH are possible Friday 
morning before strong to locally severe thunderstorm activity 
develops starting around midday and continuing through much of the
afternoon hours with major operational impacts expected due to 
gusty and erratic winds and temporary reductions in VIS and CIGs 
to MVFR/IFR conditions. Activity will move east of the terminals 
after 00z with some VCSH possible through the early evening hours.
SCT-BKN mid to high level cloud decks will prevail through 
tonight before lowering to as low as 5-6 kft by Friday morning, 
temporary lowering to as low as 3 kft in any heavier TSRA Friday 
afternoon. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No aviation weather impacts are expected throughout the TAF
period. At KIPL, westerly winds will prevail throughout the period
while at KBLH, winds will generally fluctuate between the
southeast to southwest with periods of light variability early
Friday morning. Overall speeds will remain aob 10 kts with the
exception of KIPL early Friday evening as temporary peak gusts
upwards of 20-25 kts are likely. SCT-BKN mid to high level cloud 
decks along with FEW to occasionally SCT decks around 4-7 kft will
be common throughout the period. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
After another overall dry day today, unsettled weather conditions
are expected starting Friday. Showers and thunderstorms will 
impact much of the eastern districts on Friday with heavy rainfall
likely in some areas. Minimum humidity levels today are between
20-40% before rising substantially starting Friday with widespread
45-65%. The unsettled weather and cooler temperatures will last 
through the weekend with widespread rainfall on Sunday. Outside of
any thunderstorms, winds will remain on the lighter side through 
the weekend.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Flood Watch from Saturday evening through late Sunday night for 
     AZZ534-537>563.

     Flood Watch from 6 AM MST Friday through Friday afternoon for 
     AZZ534-537>551-553>555-559.

     Flood Watch from Friday afternoon through Friday evening for 
     AZZ552-556>558-560>563.

CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Ryan/Kuhlman 
LONG TERM...Kuhlman/Ryan 
AVIATION...Lojero
